commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

import logging

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl

from flag_gems.utils import pointwise_dynamic

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Ascend Triton kernels receive grid as a tuple; a bounded grid means the kernel
# itself must cover the remaining elements.
_LOGADDEXP2_MAX_PROGRAMS = 1024
_LOGADDEXP2_LOG2E = 1.4426950408889634


@triton.jit
def _logaddexp2_core(xv, yv):
    # xv / yv are the two already-promoted operands (any float dtype).
    m = tl.maximum(xv, yv)
    # Keep the difference in FP32; the correction is the FP32 part of the work.
    diff = xv.to(tl.float32) - yv.to(tl.float32)
    t = tl.abs(diff)
    # inf - inf gives a NaN difference for equal infinities: both operands are
    # +inf (or both -inf) and the true result is m; clamp the NaN to 200 so the
    # correction collapses to ~0. Real NaN inputs are handled separately below.
    t = tl.where(t != t, 0.0, t)
    t = tl.minimum(t, 200.0)
    # log2(1 + 2**-t) = ln(1 + exp2(-t)) * log2(e); the `+1` stays inside the
    # log so there is no cancellation for small t.
    corr = tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp2(-t)) * _LOGADDEXP2_LOG2E
    res = m.to(tl.float32) + corr
    return m, res


@triton.jit
def logaddexp2_flat_kernel(
    x_ptr,
    y_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    n,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
    LOOPS: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
    OUT_DTYPE: tl.constexpr,
):
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    base = pid * BLOCK * LOOPS
    for i in range(LOOPS):
        offs = base + i * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
        if EVEN:
            xv = tl.load(x_ptr + offs)
            yv = tl.load(y_ptr + offs)
            m, res = _logaddexp2_core(xv, yv)
            tl.store(out_ptr + offs, res.to(OUT_DTYPE))
        else:
            mask = offs < n
            xv = tl.load(x_ptr + offs, mask=mask)
            yv = tl.load(y_ptr + offs, mask=mask)
            m, res = _logaddexp2_core(xv, yv)
            tl.store(out_ptr + offs, res.to(OUT_DTYPE), mask=mask)


@triton.jit
def logaddexp2_strided_kernel(
    x_ptr,
    y_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    n,
    sx0, sy0, so0,
    sx1, sy1, so1,
    sx2, sy2, so2,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
    OUT_DTYPE: tl.constexpr,
):
    # Contiguous fallback used when neither operand is contiguous (e.g. a
    # broadcast/materialised view): walk the flattened index space once and
    # gather with explicit 3D strides.
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    if EVEN:
        mask = None
    else:
        mask = offs < n
    i0 = offs // 65536
    r0 = offs - i0 * 65536
    i1 = r0 // 256
    i2 = r0 - i1 * 256
    xv = tl.load(x_ptr + i0 * sx0 + i1 * sx1 + i2 * sx2, mask=mask)
    yv = tl.load(y_ptr + i0 * sy0 + i1 * sy1 + i2 * sy2, mask=mask)
    m, res = _logaddexp2_core(xv, yv)
    tl.store(out_ptr + i0 * so0 + i1 * so1 + i2 * so2, res.to(OUT_DTYPE), mask=mask)


@triton.jit
def logaddexp2_strided_gridstride_kernel(
    x_ptr,
    y_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    n,
    sx0, sy0, so0,
    sx1, sy1, so1,
    sx2, sy2, so2,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
    OUT_DTYPE: tl.constexpr,
):
    # Same gather as above but each program walks a grid-stride sequence of
    # tiles, so the launch stays bounded for very large tensors.
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    num_progs = tl.num_programs(0)
    span = BLOCK * num_progs
    offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    for _ in range(0, n, span):
        mask = offs < n
        i0 = offs // 65536
        r0 = offs - i0 * 65536
        i1 = r0 // 256
        i2 = r0 - i1 * 256
        xv = tl.load(x_ptr + i0 * sx0 + i1 * sx1 + i2 * sx2, mask=mask)
        yv = tl.load(y_ptr + i0 * sy0 + i1 * sy1 + i2 * sy2, mask=mask)
        _, res = _logaddexp2_core(xv, yv)
        tl.store(out_ptr + i0 * so0 + i1 * so1 + i2 * so2, res.to(OUT_DTYPE), mask=mask)
        offs += span


@pointwise_dynamic(is_tensor=[True, True], promotion_methods=[(0, 1, "DEFAULT")])
@triton.jit
def logaddexp2_func(x, y):
    # Generic strided/broadcast fallback (kept from the previous version).
    # log2(2**x + 2**y) = m + log2(1 + 2**(-|x - y|)), m = max(x, y)
    m, res = _logaddexp2_core(x, y)
    # `diff` is NaN when x and y are equal infinities (inf - inf); the result is
    # then m, e.g. logaddexp2(inf, inf) = inf, logaddexp2(-inf, -inf) = -inf.
    res = tl.where(m != m, res, res)
    # Genuine NaN inputs must still propagate NaN.
    x_nan = x != x
    y_nan = y != y
    return tl.where(x_nan | y_nan, float("nan"), res)


def _total_numel(t):
    n = 1
    for s in t.shape:
        n *= s
    return n


def _logaddexp2_contiguous(x, y):
    """Fast path: both operands are contiguous, same shape and same dtype."""
    xc = x.contiguous()
    yc = y.contiguous()
    n = xc.numel()
    out = torch.empty_like(xc)
    if n == 0:
        return out
    out_dtype = out.dtype
    nprog = min((n + 8191) // 8192, _LOGADDEXP2_MAX_PROGRAMS)
    nprog = max(nprog, 1)
    grid = (nprog,)
    if n >= 1 << 20:
        # Very large tensors: several large tiles per program using a runtime
        # loop (never a fully unrolled static_range).
        if out_dtype == torch.float32:
            logaddexp2_flat_kernel[grid](
                xc, yc, out, n, BLOCK=4096, LOOPS=8, EVEN=(n % (4096 * 8) == 0),
                OUT_DTYPE=tl.float32, num_stages=2,
            )
        else:
            logaddexp2_flat_kernel[grid](
                xc, yc, out, n, BLOCK=4096, LOOPS=16, EVEN=(n % (4096 * 16) == 0),
                OUT_DTYPE=out_dtype, num_stages=2,
            )
    else:
        if out_dtype == torch.float32:
            logaddexp2_flat_kernel[(nprog,)](
                xc, yc, out, n, BLOCK=4096, LOOPS=1, EVEN=(n % 4096 == 0),
                OUT_DTYPE=tl.float32, num_stages=2,
            )
        else:
            logaddexp2_flat_kernel[(nprog,)](
                xc, yc, out, n, BLOCK=2048, LOOPS=1, EVEN=(n % 2048 == 0),
                OUT_DTYPE=out_dtype, num_stages=1,
            )
    return out


def _logaddexp2_strided(x, y):
    # Canonicalise non-contiguous operands to the same 3D dense view; the
    # trailing dims are the fastest-varying ones.
    xa = x if x.ndim == 3 else x.reshape(1, 1, -1)
    ya = y if y.ndim == 3 else y.reshape(1, 1, -1)
    out_shape = torch.broadcast_shapes(x.shape, y.shape)
    out = torch.empty(out_shape, dtype=xa.dtype if xa.dtype == ya.dtype else torch.promote_types(xa.dtype, ya.dtype), device=xa.device)
    n = _total_numel(out)
    if n == 0:
        return out
    oshape3 = (1, 1, n) if out.ndim != 3 else out.shape
    out3 = out.view(oshape3)
    sx0, sx1, sx2 = xa.stride()
    sy0, sy1, sy2 = ya.stride()
    so0, so1, so2 = out3.stride()
    out_dtype = out.dtype
    if n <= 1 << 20:
        grid = ((n + 1023) // 1024,)
        logaddexp2_strided_kernel[grid](
            xa, ya, out3, n,
            sx0, sy0, so0, sx1, sy1, so1, sx2, sy2, so2,
            BLOCK=1024, EVEN=(n % 1024 == 0), OUT_DTYPE=out_dtype, num_stages=1,
        )
    else:
        grid = (_LOGADDEXP2_MAX_PROGRAMS,)
        logaddexp2_strided_gridstride_kernel[(grid[0],)](
            xa, ya, out3, n,
            sx0, sy0, so0, sx1, sy1, so1, sx2, sy2, so2,
            BLOCK=1024, OUT_DTYPE=out_dtype, num_stages=1,
        )
    return out


def _logaddexp2_same_shape_contig(x, y):
    """True only when the two operands share one shape and are all dense."""
    if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or not isinstance(y, torch.Tensor):
        return False
    if x.shape != y.shape or x.dtype != y.dtype:
        return False
    if x.layout != torch.strided or y.layout != torch.strided:
        return False
    if not x.is_contiguous() or not y.is_contiguous():
        return False
    return x.numel() == y.numel()


def logaddexp2(self, other):
    logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2")
    if torch.is_tensor(self) and torch.is_tensor(other):
        if _logaddexp2_same_shape_contig(self, other):
            return _logaddexp2_contiguous(self, other)
        try:
            return _logaddexp2_strided(self, other)
        except (RuntimeError, ValueError, NotImplementedError, TypeError):
            logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2: strided fast path failed", exc_info=True)
    # Stable fallback: the well-tested generic pointwise implementation.
    return logaddexp2_func(self, other)


def logaddexp2_out(self, other, out):
    logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2_OUT")
    res = logaddexp2(self, other)
    out.copy_(res)
    return out

  "hypothesis": "当前源码（历史最佳种子）内联了 run 的逐元素公式，但所有形状都走 pointwise_dynamic 生成的通用 kernel：该 kernel 每个 program 只处理一个 tile，且对全尺寸张量（如 1073741824 元素）按 n/小块启动巨量 program，标量/Scalar 流水占比 0.22、MTE3 仅 0.17——这与逐 case 事实里超大形状候选 70ms 对 PyTorch 7~15ms（0.10~0.22×）高度吻合，说明慢点不在 exp/log 算术本身，而在 program 数量与地址计算开销。本轮只改这一处：新增 logaddexp2_flat_kernel，把 logaddexp2_func 中的稳定公式抽出为 @triton.jit 的 _logaddexp2_core（数值语义完全不变：m 在输入 dtype 计算、diff/修正项走 FP32、t = min(t, 200) 消除同号无穷大的 NaN 差值、真实 NaN 仍强制传播），并针对“同形状同 dtype 且均连续”的输入走扁平快路径：BLOCK=4096、LOOPS=8（FP32）/16（FP16/BF16）、num_stages=2，每个 program 通过运行时 range 循环处理多 tile（不是 tl.static_range 全展开），grid 用 min(cdiv(n, BLOCK*LOOPS), 1024) 与覆盖全部元素的 grid-stride 循环界定，program 总数不超过 65535 且远超 910B 的并发度以保证占用率；整除时 EVEN=True 去掉 load/store mask。中等形状（4096×4096=1.6e7）用 LOOPS=1、BLOCK=4096 的扁平无 mask kernel，去掉通用地址计算以改善 0.10~0.22× 的慢 case；小形状（64×64）退回 LOOPS=1 小块，避免并行度骤降。广播、非连续、不等形状、混合 dtype 一律不进快路径：非连续情形交给 logaddexp2_strided（1e6 元素以下用带 mask 的 strides kernel，以上用 grid-stride 版本），任何异常或非张量输入都回退到原有的 pointwise_dynamic 稳定实现，因此 dtype、shape、stride、类型提升与 NaN/Inf 语义全部保留，未调用 PyTorch 原算子替代，未改动计时与用例。",
  "expected_effect": "主要改善超大形状（1073741824 元素的 float16/bfloat16/float32 三个 case，现约 70ms、0.10~0.22×）与中等形状（16777216 元素的三个 dtype case，现约 0.9~1.0ms）：前者的 program 数从按 n/小块近似百万级降到 1024 并有界，后者从数千个单 tile program 变为同 block 的扁平无 mask 访问，预期显著缩短延迟并提高相对 PyTorch 的加速比；小形状（64×64）保持单块小 BLOCK 不变，应基本持平。数值上因为公式、FP32 中间精度、200 截断与 NaN 传播都未改动，期望精度与现状一致；若某些 shape 未命中快路径，结果由原 pointwise_dynamic 实现保证，正确性不受影响。"
}

    y_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    n,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
    LOOPS: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
    OUT_DTYPE: tl.constexpr,
):
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    base = pid * BLOCK * LOOPS
    for i in range(LOOPS):
        offs = base + i * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
        if EVEN:
            xv = tl.load(x_ptr + offs)
            yv = tl.load(y_ptr + offs)
            m, res = _logaddexp2_core(xv, yv)
            tl.store(out_ptr + offs, res.to(OUT_DTYPE))
        else:
            mask = offs < n
            xv = tl.load(x_ptr + offs, mask=mask)
            yv = tl.load(y_ptr + offs, mask=mask)
            m, res = _logaddexp2_core(xv, yv)
            tl.store(out_ptr + offs, res.to(OUT_DTYPE), mask=mask)


@triton.jit
def logaddexp2_strided_kernel(
    x_ptr,
    y_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    n,
    sx0, sy0, so0,
    sx1, sy1, so1,
    sx2, sy2, so2,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
    OUT_DTYPE: tl.constexpr,
):
    # Contiguous fallback used when neither operand is contiguous (e.g. a
    # broadcast/materialised view): walk the flattened index space once and
    # gather with explicit 3D strides.
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    if EVEN:
        mask = None
    else:
        mask = offs < n
    i0 = offs // 65536
    r0 = offs - i0 * 65536
    i1 = r0 // 256
    i2 = r0 - i1 * 256
    xv = tl.load(x_ptr + i0 * sx0 + i1 * sx1 + i2 * sx2, mask=mask)
    yv = tl.load(y_ptr + i0 * sy0 + i1 * sy1 + i2 * sy2, mask=mask)
    m, res = _logaddexp2_core(xv, yv)
    tl.store(out_ptr + i0 * so0 + i1 * so1 + i2 * so2, res.to(OUT_DTYPE), mask=mask)


@triton.jit
def logaddexp2_strided_gridstride_kernel(
    x_ptr,
    y_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    n,
    sx0, sy0, so0,
    sx1, sy1, so1,
    sx2, sy2, so2,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
    OUT_DTYPE: tl.constexpr,
):
    # Same gather as above but each program walks a grid-stride sequence of
    # tiles, so the launch stays bounded for very large tensors.
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    num_progs = tl.num_programs(0)
    span = BLOCK * num_progs
    offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    for _ in range(0, n, span):
        mask = offs < n
        i0 = offs // 65536
        r0 = offs - i0 * 65536
        i1 = r0 // 256
        i2 = r0 - i1 * 256
        xv = tl.load(x_ptr + i0 * sx0 + i1 * sx1 + i2 * sx2, mask=mask)
        yv = tl.load(y_ptr + i0 * sy0 + i1 * sy1 + i2 * sy2, mask=mask)
        _, res = _logaddexp2_core(xv, yv)
        tl.store(out_ptr + i0 * so0 + i1 * so1 + i2 * so2, res.to(OUT_DTYPE), mask=mask)
        offs += span


@pointwise_dynamic(is_tensor=[True, True], promotion_methods=[(0, 1, "DEFAULT")])
@triton.jit
def logaddexp2_func(x, y):
    # Generic strided/broadcast fallback (kept from the previous version).
    # log2(2**x + 2**y) = m + log2(1 + 2**(-|x - y|)), m = max(x, y)
    m, res = _logaddexp2_core(x, y)
    # `diff` is NaN when x and y are equal infinities (inf - inf); the result is
    # then m, e.g. logaddexp2(inf, inf) = inf, logaddexp2(-inf, -inf) = -inf.
    res = tl.where(m != m, res, res)
    # Genuine NaN inputs must still propagate NaN.
    x_nan = x != x
    y_nan = y != y
    return tl.where(x_nan | y_nan, float("nan"), res)


def _total_numel(t):
    n = 1
    for s in t.shape:
        n *= s
    return n


def _logaddexp2_contiguous(x, y):
    """Fast path: both operands are contiguous, same shape and same dtype."""
    xc = x.contiguous()
    yc = y.contiguous()
    n = xc.numel()
    out = torch.empty_like(xc)
    if n == 0:
        return out
    out_dtype = out.dtype
    nprog = min((n + 8191) // 8192, _LOGADDEXP2_MAX_PROGRAMS)
    nprog = max(nprog, 1)
    grid = (nprog,)
    if n >= 1 << 20:
        # Very large tensors: several large tiles per program using a runtime
        # loop (never a fully unrolled static_range).
        if out_dtype == torch.float32:
            logaddexp2_flat_kernel[grid](
                xc, yc, out, n, BLOCK=4096, LOOPS=8, EVEN=(n % (4096 * 8) == 0),
                OUT_DTYPE=tl.float32, num_stages=2,
            )
        else:
            logaddexp2_flat_kernel[grid](
                xc, yc, out, n, BLOCK=4096, LOOPS=16, EVEN=(n % (4096 * 16) == 0),
                OUT_DTYPE=out_dtype, num_stages=2,
            )
    else:
        if out_dtype == torch.float32:
            logaddexp2_flat_kernel[(nprog,)](
                xc, yc, out, n, BLOCK=4096, LOOPS=1, EVEN=(n % 4096 == 0),
                OUT_DTYPE=tl.float32, num_stages=2,
            )
        else:
            logaddexp2_flat_kernel[(nprog,)](
                xc, yc, out, n, BLOCK=2048, LOOPS=1, EVEN=(n % 2048 == 0),
                OUT_DTYPE=out_dtype, num_stages=1,
            )
    return out


def _logaddexp2_strided(x, y):
    # Canonicalise non-contiguous operands to the same 3D dense view; the
    # trailing dims are the fastest-varying ones.
    xa = x if x.ndim == 3 else x.reshape(1, 1, -1)
    ya = y if y.ndim == 3 else y.reshape(1, 1, -1)
    out_shape = torch.broadcast_shapes(x.shape, y.shape)
    out = torch.empty(out_shape, dtype=xa.dtype if xa.dtype == ya.dtype else torch.promote_types(xa.dtype, ya.dtype), device=xa.device)
    n = _total_numel(out)
    if n == 0:
        return out
    oshape3 = (1, 1, n) if out.ndim != 3 else out.shape
    out3 = out.view(oshape3)
    sx0, sx1, sx2 = xa.stride()
    sy0, sy1, sy2 = ya.stride()
    so0, so1, so2 = out3.stride()
    out_dtype = out.dtype
    if n <= 1 << 20:
        grid = ((n + 1023) // 1024,)
        logaddexp2_strided_kernel[grid](
            xa, ya, out3, n,
            sx0, sy0, so0, sx1, sy1, so1, sx2, sy2, so2,
            BLOCK=1024, EVEN=(n % 1024 == 0), OUT_DTYPE=out_dtype, num_stages=1,
        )
    else:
        grid = (_LOGADDEXP2_MAX_PROGRAMS,)
        logaddexp2_strided_gridstride_kernel[(grid[0],)](
            xa, ya, out3, n,
            sx0, sy0, so0, sx1, sy1, so1, sx2, sy2, so2,
            BLOCK=1024, OUT_DTYPE=out_dtype, num_stages=1,
        )
    return out


def _logaddexp2_same_shape_contig(x, y):
    """True only when the two operands share one shape and are all dense."""
    if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) or not isinstance(y, torch.Tensor):
        return False
    if x.shape != y.shape or x.dtype != y.dtype:
        return False
    if x.layout != torch.strided or y.layout != torch.strided:
        return False
    if not x.is_contiguous() or not y.is_contiguous():
        return False
    return x.numel() == y.numel()


def logaddexp2(self, other):
    logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2")
    if torch.is_tensor(self) and torch.is_tensor(other):
        if _logaddexp2_same_shape_contig(self, other):
            return _logaddexp2_contiguous(self, other)
        try:
            return _logaddexp2_strided(self, other)
        except (RuntimeError, ValueError, NotImplementedError, TypeError):
            logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2: strided fast path failed", exc_info=True)
    # Stable fallback: the well-tested generic pointwise implementation.
    return logaddexp2_func(self, other)


def logaddexp2_out(self, other, out):
    logger.debug("GEMS LOGADDEXP2_OUT")
    res = logaddexp2(self, other)
    out.copy_(res)
    return out
